facts.about: Polycab is India’s leading manufacturers of cables and wires and allied products such as uPVC conduits and lugs and glands. We have a range of cables and wires for practically every application. More recently Polycab has also launched a wide range of consumer electrical products like Fans, Switches, Switchgear, LED lights and Luminaries, Solar Inverters, and Pumps.

flags.text: Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 101% of PAT
Receivable days stretched from 32 to 48 in 3 years
Latest quarter growth (+53%) accelerating vs 3-yr trend (+27%)

business.summary: Polycab India Limited manufactures and sells wires, cables, and fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG), while also executing electrical infrastructure projects. It generates revenue through domestic and international sales of these electrical solutions across retail, industrial, and institutional sectors.

segments.name: Wires and Cables
segments.note: Leading Indian manufacturer supplying diverse retail, industrial, and institutional customers.

segments.name: Fast-Moving Electrical Goods (FMEG)
segments.note: Delivers innovative solutions including fans, lighting, switches, and appliances.

segments.name: Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC)
segments.note: Executes complex electrical infrastructure projects for government and institutional customers.

scorecard.promised: Sustain medium- to long-term EBITDA margins within 11% to 13% range.
scorecard.delivered: Delivered 14% margin in Sep 2026 and 14% for full year Mar 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Margins have consistently stayed at or above the 11-13% range, hitting 14% in the latest quarter.

scorecard.promised: Grow at 1.5x to 2x of the industry growth rate.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue grew 52.8% YoY in Sep 2026; annual revenue reached ₹28,884 cr.
scorecard.evidence: Growth accelerated from 26.9% in Mar 2026 to 52.8% in Sep 2026, likely exceeding industry averages.

scorecard.promised: Execute INR 60 billion to INR 80 billion capex over 5 years.
scorecard.delivered: 9M FY26 capex was ₹10.9 billion; CWIP stands at ₹1,401 cr.
scorecard.evidence: Annual run-rate of ₹12-16bn is being maintained to reach the 5-year target.

scorecard.promised: Normalize to 50 to 55 days (later revised to 45-50 days).
scorecard.delivered: Cash conversion cycle improved to 39 days as of Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Management beat their own 45-50 day target, reaching 39 days from 65 days three years ago.

scorecard.promised: Targeting EBITDA margins in the range of 8% to 10% by FY30.
scorecard.delivered: FMEG margin reached 10.1% in Q2 FY27.
scorecard.evidence: Current 10.1% margin already meets the FY30 target of 8-10% ahead of schedule.

narrative.scoreline: Management has consistently over-delivered on margin and working capital targets while maintaining aggressive revenue growth acceleration.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: FMEG margin expansion to 10.1% was driven by scale and operating leverage.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue grew 52.8% in the latest quarter, supporting the scale narrative.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Domestic wires and cable organized market share increased to 30-31%.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue grew from ₹18,039 cr (Mar 2024) to ₹28,884 cr (Mar 2026), supporting share gain claims.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Higher inventory days in Q3 FY26 were for pre-stocking for Q4 demand.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue jumped from ₹7,636 cr in Dec 2025 to ₹8,864 cr in Mar 2026.

bull: Revenue growth is accelerating, hitting 52.8% YoY in Sep 2026 versus a 27% 3-year trend.
Cash generation is elite, with 5-year operating cash flow at 101% of PAT.
FMEG segment has achieved its FY30 margin target of 8-10% four years early.
bear: Receivable days have stretched from 32 to 48 days over the last three years.
EHV plant commissioning has been pushed out to FY2028.
Auditors flagged EPC contract cost estimation as a key audit matter, posing margin risks.
watch: Check if Sep 2026's 52.8% revenue growth rate sustains or mean-reverts next quarter.
Monitor if receivable days continue to climb beyond the current 48 days.
Verify if FMEG margins stay above 10% without sacrificing volume growth.

claims.claim: Margin expansion to 10.1% was driven by scale, operating leverage, and an increased premium product mix.
claims.quote: Now, definitely scale has increased in this quarter... I think the scale definitely plays an important part, and definitely the operating leverage from here. The second part... is premium mix has also gone up.

claims.claim: We do not see any real competition in the near term as the wires market is small.
claims.quote: But however, we don't see any real competition in the near term, simply because that wires market is still very small part of our overall business.

claims.claim: We do not expect any adverse or material impact on our financial or business operations.
claims.quote: We do not expect any adverse or material impact on our financial or business operations arising from the said situation.

claims.claim: The EHV plant is expected to be commissioned in FY28.
claims.quote: So I would like to take this opportunity to sort of also let the investor community know that in terms of our EHV plant timelines, we are expecting the EHV plant to now commission somewhere in FY 2028.

claims.claim: We expect the working capital cycle to settle within our long-term operating range of 45 to 50 days.
claims.quote: As these effects normalize, we expect the working capital cycle to settle within our long-term operating range of 45 to 50 days.

claims.claim: We have already secured the fibre for the execution period, which is next 2 to 3 years.
claims.quote: Happy to state that the strength of our procurement is such that we have been able to secure the fibre for the execution period, which is next 2 to 3 years.

claims.claim: In last quarter, in fact, we updated that overall, we have gained 3% to 4% market share.
claims.quote: In last quarter, in fact, we updated that overall, we have gained 3% to 4% market share.

claims.claim: Our domestic wires and cable organized market share has increased to 30-31%.
claims.quote: Our domestic wires and cable organized market share has now increased to 30-31% up from 18-19% in financial year 2019.

claims.claim: We do not have inventory gains because we use a hedging mechanism for raw materials.
claims.quote: we have a hedging mechanism in place. So we don't have any inventory gain unlike peers.

claims.claim: Power sector, manufacturing, and infrastructure projects will continue to drive strong demand for cables and wires.
claims.quote: Sectors like utilities, metals, semiconductors, oil and gas, manufacturing, logistics, all of this is going to convert into strong demand for Cable & Wire.

claims.claim: Staggered pass-through of commodity inflation was a strategic choice to protect volumes and market share.
claims.quote: In order to avoid demand disruption, arising from elevated input costs, the Company took a strategic decision to pass on the increase in raw material prices in a staggered manner.

claims.claim: Higher inventory days are due to pre-stocking in anticipation of strong Q4 demand.
claims.quote: On working capital front, same as last quarter, inventory days continue to be higher as we built up inventory in anticipation of strong demand in Q4 FY26.

claims.claim: FMEG segment remained profitable for the fourth consecutive quarter despite increased A&P investments.
claims.quote: Importantly, the FMEG segment remained profitable for the fourth consecutive quarter, even while strategically ramping up our A&P investments to strengthen brand presence and drive long-term growth.

risks.text: Contingent liabilities include various disputed tax demands and export obligation commitments.
Related party transactions are conducted on an arm's length basis in the ordinary course of business.
Auditors identified revenue recognition and EPC contract cost estimation as key audit matters.
